units.text: Follow the central bundle. A link aggregation group uses LACP to combine dedicated connections at one Direct Connect endpoint into a managed logical interface. The group simplifies configuration and increases available capacity.

Compare the upper callouts. Member connections use the same bandwidth and terminate at the same endpoint. They therefore share endpoint and location exposure; more members do not create location diversity.

Read the lower-left setting. Minimum active links defines when the logical group remains operational. Set the threshold deliberately so losing members does not leave an overloaded path appearing usable.

With the full diagram visible, inspect the lower-right flows. Distribution across members does not guarantee aggregate bandwidth for one flow. Test workload behavior and use independent locations when location-failure protection is required.

Start with the first column. Choose independent Direct Connect paths or an internet VPN backup according to the workload requirements. Confirm that the backup avoids the failure affecting the primary.
Move to the second column. Advertise and select routes deliberately. A more-specific route can defeat the intended primary path, so check the actual forward and return decisions.

Inspect the capacity gauge in the third column. Size the backup for critical workloads and plan to defer noncritical transfers. A connected backup is insufficient when it cannot carry essential demand.

Review the full slide and the final checklist. During a real failover test, measure routing convergence, application reconnection and recovery. Define an acceptable degraded mode and verify it under representative load.
Begin with TLS on the left. It protects application sessions between the TLS endpoints. Identify where those sessions terminate before deciding which sections of the application path are protected.
Move to IPsec. Its protection runs between VPN tunnel endpoints. Traffic outside that tunnel boundary needs any additional protection required by the design.
Compare MACsec in the third panel. It protects a supported Layer Two point-to-point link. That link boundary is different from application end-to-end encryption and does not replace it automatically.
Return to the full slide and the Direct Connect panel. Direct Connect traffic is not encrypted by default. Choose and verify encryption for the specific boundary that the workload requires.

Follow the upper-left chain. Private IP Site-to-Site VPN can run over Direct Connect using a transit virtual interface, a Direct Connect gateway and Transit Gateway. These components provide the underlying transport.

Inspect the center tunnel and upper-right panel. VPN endpoints use private addresses, while IPsec protects application traffic between the tunnel endpoints. Private addressing and encryption still have distinct roles.

Read the lower-left layers. The underlay supplies reachability between VPN endpoints. Overlay route advertisements carry application prefixes across the VPN. Keep those routing purposes separate to avoid recursive paths.

With the full source slide visible, use the lower-right checklist. Verify endpoint reachability, VPN capacity, feature compatibility and failover. An encrypted overlay cannot remain available when its required underlying transport fails.
